links.note: Where the child gets the flowers for the boats - from their garden. The shiuli flowers of 28284, not the stream journey.
When the poet hopes the blooms will be carried safely to land - in the night. About the shiuli 'blooms of the dawn' themselves.
What the lading in the fairies' baskets is - baskets full of dreams. The imagined journey of the boats downstream and on into the night.
The cargo carried by the fairies of sleep - the dream stage of the boats' journey, which is 28282.
The significance of the fairies and dreams in the final stanza - the child's imagined continuation of the boats' voyage.
What the child looks up at after launching the boats - the sky. Part of the launching-and-watching sequence in 28282.
What the child imagines the clouds doing - setting the white bulging sails, racing his boats. The imagined journey.
What the child does when night comes - buries his face in his arms and dreams the boats sail on. The journey continued in sleep.
What the 'lading' carried by the fairies of sleep is - baskets full of dreams. The night half of the boats' voyage.
What writing the name and village on the boats symbolises - connection. The purpose of sending them down the stream.
What the poet does when night comes - buries his face in his arms and dreams. The imagined onward journey.
Whether Shaana's Appa and Amma enjoyed themselves like children, with evidence from the text - read across the series of dated letters, which is 28290.
What less snow in the glaciers and more flooding in the Sundarbans indicate - an inference drawn across two separate letters in the series.
The author's purpose in presenting the text as postcards - exactly 28290, the text being a series of letters written from a journey.
Table of Places Visited against descriptions and activities - built by reading the whole sequence of dated letters from different states.
Where Shaana lived - Rameswaram. The home the letters are written back to.
Who Shaana went on the vacation with - Appa. The family journey the letters report.
Which activity Shaana did NOT do - Zumba. Answerable only by reading across the whole series of letters.
Where Shaana lives - Rameswaram island, the point the journey starts from and returns to.
The Pamban bridge crossed before reaching home - the last leg of the journey the letters trace.
Where Shaana lives and what she is doing with her parents - travelling the length and breadth of the country, which is the premise of 28290.
How long the journey from West Bengal to Gujarat took - two-and-a-half days. A leg of the journey between two letters.
How they travelled from West Bengal to Gujarat - not mentioned in the letters. A question about what the letters do and do not say.
Shaana's score in the surprise test, 88% - a detail reported in one of the letters, not a place description.
The name of the bridge on which the train crossed the sea - Pamban. The homeward leg of the journey.
How Shaana reached Himachal Pradesh - by train. The mode of travel between two letters in the series.
Where Shaana hoped to see red pandas - Arunachal Pradesh. What that place was like, as described in its letter.
Where Shaana saw crocodiles - the Sunderbans. A described feature of that place.
The climate in the desert - hot and dry. The letter's description of the place.
Why Shaana's hands were shaking - she wasn't wearing gloves at the glacier. A detail of the place as she describes it.
Where the Thajiwas glacier is - Kashmir. Locating a place from its own letter's description.
They went boating on a river in the Sunderbans - what that place offered, as described.
What amazed Shaana at the Sunderbans - mangrove trees growing in the sea. The distinctive feature of that place.
Which glacier she visited in Kashmir - Thajiwas, white and blue. The described place.
Amma saying Appa's snoring sounded like bears growling - from the Himachal cabin at night, which 28291 names directly.
Which state had the very thick forest - Arunachal Pradesh. The place as her letter describes it.
What trees grow in seawater in the Sunderbans - mangroves. A described feature of the place.
What Shaana used to be afraid of - tunnels, from the Goa letter describing the train through the plateaus.
Her first destination and what she observed - white and blue glaciers, less snow than last year. Describing the place.
How she reached Himachal and what she heard there - colourful birds waking her. 28291 names the birds that wake her at sunrise.
